newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices fall as speculators take profits.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices fall as speculators take profits.

text.p: Oil prices fell on Tuesday under pressure from speculators who expect a recent bull run to end if figures later in the day show larger U.S. stocks of heating oil ready for winter.
On the London futures exchange the December futures contract for world benchmark Brent Blend crude from the North Sea ended the day down 44 cents at $23.73 a barrel.
"I think the trend has reversed in the short-term...It's looking toppy and a lot of people see a build in the heating oil stocks," a broker said.
Physical Brent was abundant -- a cargo traded late on Tuesday 37 cents below a similar deal on Monday.
Traders said North Sea sweet crudes such as Brent needed to move out of Europe to rebalance the market.

The American Petroleum Institute is due to release weekly stock data, which brokers expect will show a build-up in both crude and heating oil inventories, which have so far been well below last year's levels.
Two big U.S. trading companies were the biggest sellers, possibly taking speculative short positions, brokers said.
Oil prices have rallied to a near six-month high partly because industry stocks were low.
The continued absence of supplies from embargoed Iraq also fed the rally but some analysts believe an oil-for-food deal postponed in May could be implemented after America's presidential election.

"With the U.S. elections next week, the last major hurdle to the Iraqi humanitarian deal going through is removed. After next week you could hear more Iraqi crude oil talk again," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache Securities.

A former Iraqi oil minister, Issam Chalabi, told an oil conference that at current oil prices, Iraq would export only 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude as opposed to the 700,000-800,000 bpd the market anticipated when prices were lower.
